result.description:
Based in Noosa, Australia, we've partnered with some of the world's largest corporations in personal care and agriculture to deliver our first-of-a-kind products, and we are now rapidly scaling operations to meet increasing demand.

 

We're seeking an exceptional Aquaculture Consultant (Production Technician) with experience in microalgae cultivation to join our growing production team, focused on the large-scale production of microalgae in our recirculating production facilities. This is a hands-on, science-led role: you'll apply aquaculture and environmental-science expertise to optimise cultivation and downstream processing, develop and refine protocols, and drive data-driven improvements across our operations. Based in Noosa, and working alongside world-leading experts in a purpose-driven, highly motivated team, you'll be supported with on-the-job training to help you become a world leader in the field, with opportunities for rapid career progression.

 

Key responsibilities

Maintain and optimise large-scale microalgae cultures across manual, semi-automated and fully automated systems.
Apply aquaculture and environmental-science principles to evaluate culture health, water quality and growth conditions, and identify solutions for production issues and environmental impacts.
Operate closed-system bioreactors in compliance with internal protocols and specified regulatory standards.
Study, conduct and improve downstream processing activities from harvest through to the final product.
Contribute to the ongoing development, optimisation and scientific documentation of the algae production process.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve production efficiency.
Maintain precise, accurate records to support data-driven improvements, regulatory compliance and conservation.
Skills and experience required

A degree in environmental science, marine or aquatic science, aquaculture, bioprocessing, biotechnology or a related field (or equivalent industry experience).
Demonstrated experience in microalgae/seaweed cultivation, aquaculture or large-scale biomanufacturing.
Working knowledge of bioprocessing, downstream processing and quality/record-keeping systems.
A problem-solving, can-do attitude.
Strong communication and reporting skills.
What we offer

A competitive salary of AUD $80,000–$90,000 plus superannuation.
A team-first work environment that supports personal and professional growth.
The opportunity to contribute to meaningful, purpose-driven solutions for some of the world's biggest problems.
A diverse and inclusive workplace, with a commitment to continuous learning and innovation.
Monthly team events.
Our company values

Pioneering: embrace curiosity and innovation.
Collaborative: be transparent, honest, and open to feedback.
Decisive: make bold, data-driven decisions.
Accountable: own your work and results.
Fun: create a workplace where people enjoy their work.

To Apply please navigate to our website and apply via the careers page.

Job title:  Speech Pathologist - Clinic/Community - Edgecliff, NSW 

  Hours:  16 - 38 hours/week, Flexible 

  Salary:   Excellent pay + Travel Allowances + CPD + Benefits 

  Location:  Edgecliff, NSW 

   

  About the company:  

 Our client is a dedicated team of therapists providing comprehensive care and support to children and their families on their therapy journey. Specializing in children aged 0-18, they utilize a holistic and evidence-based approach, working collaboratively with families, educators, and other health professionals to ensure each child flourishes and reaches their full potential. Their services encompass a range of therapeutic interventions, including support for sensory, motor, social, cognitive, and learning difficulties, as well as speech and language development. With a focus on kindness, fairness, optimism, and trust, they strive to empower children, building their confidence, resilience, and independence. Services are offered both in their Edgecliff clinic and through mobile visits to homes, schools, and childcare centers across Sydney. They are committed to providing leading-edge interventions, utilizing the latest assessment tools and high-quality resources. 

   

  About the Role:  

 Our client is looking for an enthusiastic Speech Pathologist   to join their multidisciplinary supportive team. As a Speech Pathologist you will be: 

 
	  Screenings:  This position involves performing individual, observation-based speech and language screenings with preschool and kindergarten children in various settings such as preschools, daycare centers, and schools. The screenings will evaluate age-appropriate speech and language development, with a focus on determining school readiness. The results of these screenings, along with any recommendations, will then be communicated to both the children's families and their educators. 
	  Assessments:  This process involves comprehensive developmental assessments for children, conducted in various settings like clinics, daycare centers, schools, or homes. Evaluations utilize standardized and non-standardized assessments, along with clinical observations. Information gathering includes parent phone consultations, questionnaires for parents and teachers, and review of medical records. Initial assessments last 60-90 minutes, and formal reports with recommendations are prepared within 10 days, shared with relevant parties upon consent. Finally, the assessor collaborates with parents to create individualized goals and provides classroom strategies and resources to educators. 
	  Intervention & Ongoing Care:  Regular review assessments should be conducted to track progress toward established goals. Progress reports should be provided after each assessment and also be made available to parents and educators upon request. Finally, children should be discharged from services once they have achieved their designated goals.
